b1-cambiosocial-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Cities Around 1900
b1-cambiosocial-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are at a museum exhibition about Buenos Aires around 1900, and Carlos asks what the city was like.
b1-cambiosocial-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what Buenos Aires was like.
cues: Say that the city grew every year
Say that the cities had trams
b1-cambiosocial-01.target: Buenos Aires crecía todos los años. Las ciudades tenían tranvías.
b1-cambiosocial-01.english: Buenos Aires grew every year. The cities had trams.
b1-cambiosocial-01.canDo: I can say how Buenos Aires and other cities grew.

b1-cambiosocial-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The New Middle Class
b1-cambiosocial-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading a book about the new social classes, and Meg asks what the middle class wanted.
b1-cambiosocial-02.prompt: Tell Meg what historians say about the middle class.
cues: Name the source of the information
Say what the middle class asked for
b1-cambiosocial-02.target: Según los historiadores, la clase media pedía más participación política.
b1-cambiosocial-02.english: According to historians, the middle class was asking for more political participation.
b1-cambiosocial-02.canDo: I can say who belonged to the new middle class.

b1-cambiosocial-03.title: Communicative Challenge: How They Found Work
b1-cambiosocial-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a class on immigration, and Carlos asks how immigrants found out about work.
b1-cambiosocial-03.prompt: Tell Carlos how many immigrants got information about work.
cues: Say how they got the information
b1-cambiosocial-03.target: Muchos conseguían información sobre el trabajo a través de cartas de familiares y amigos.
b1-cambiosocial-03.english: Many got information about work through letters from relatives and friends.
b1-cambiosocial-03.canDo: I can say where most immigrants came from and where they went.

b1-cambiosocial-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Strike in Mexico
b1-cambiosocial-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg watched a documentary about strikes in Mexico, and Meg asks what happened in Río Blanco.
b1-cambiosocial-04.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to the strike of 1907.
cues: Say what happened to the strike
b1-cambiosocial-04.target: La huelga de 1907 fue reprimida por el ejército.
b1-cambiosocial-04.english: The strike of 1907 was put down by the army.
b1-cambiosocial-04.canDo: I can say what workers asked for and who led the unions.

b1-cambiosocial-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Women and the Vote
b1-cambiosocial-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a book on women in Latin America, and Carlos asks what women could do around 1900.
b1-cambiosocial-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what women could and could not do.
cues: Say that women could not vote
Say that many worked as teachers
b1-cambiosocial-05.target: Aunque las mujeres no podían votar, muchas trabajaban como maestras.
b1-cambiosocial-05.english: Although women could not vote, many worked as teachers.
b1-cambiosocial-05.canDo: I can say what the university reform of Córdoba asked for.

b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Learned About Social Change
b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a class on social change, and Carlos asks what the workers wanted.
b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the workers asked for.
cues: Say what they did when the boss did not accept
b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.target: Los obreros pedían salarios más altos y hacían huelga.
b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.english: The workers asked for higher wages and went on strike.
b1-cambiosocial-consolidation.canDo: I can describe how the cities of Latin America changed around 1900.
